text: More than 200 layoffs planned at tech, manufacturing companies in Essex and Camden Advance Local Express Desk, Stephanie  Loder June 29, 2026 1 min read IP ADP Two employers are eyeing more than 200 job cuts at their New Jersey facilities by early fall, according to notices filed Monday. Automatic Data Processing Inc. , known as ADP and headquartered in Roseland, and International Paper's box plant in Barrington together account for 202 affected workers in notices filed under the federal Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification Act. The job cuts are scheduled to take effect in late September. ADP reported 76 employees will be impacted at its Roseland headquarters, with layoffs effective Sept. 25. International Paper reported a significant reduction at its Barrington container plant, where 126 workers are slated to lose their jobs effective Sept. 24. ADP, a multinational provider of cloud-based human capital management software and services, employs roughly 67,000 people globally and operates in more than 140 countries. The Roseland-based company is a dominant force in payroll and HR technology. The company's core offerings include cloud-based HR platforms, payroll and tax administration, benefits management and professional employer organization services. The Memphis-based packaging manufacturer produces corrugated containers and fiber-based packaging used across shipping, retail and industrial supply chains. Its Barrington plant, located on East Gloucester Pike, serves regional and national markets as part of the company's North American manufacturing network. International Paper employs more than 10,000 people and supplies packaging for consumer goods and e-commerce distribution. The New Jersey WARN filings provide advance notice of mass layoffs or plant closures, giving workers and local officials time to prepare for employment impacts.
